label: copy-phase input v (fed-back original token at position >= 2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is v, and only once the copy has reached recall_idx >= 3, so the v being re-read is original position 2 or later. It never fires in the original phase or at <DEL>, and essentially never on any input token other than v. On copy-phase v at recall_idx 1 or 2 (original positions 0-1) it is silent or weak: about 0.4% rate at recall_idx 2, and these weak hits make up most of the lowest-quartile misses. Magnitude is larger later in the sequence: in the top examples the v is near the end of the copy (to_go 0-1). Out_tok, prev tokens, first token and L have little effect beyond this position effect. Dev F1 0.98, precision 0.998.

issues: Minor factual slip: the explanation says v fed back at recall_idx 2 has an 'about 0.4% rate'. That 0.4% is the rate across all inputs at recall_idx 2. For v specifically at recall_idx 2, the feature fires about 12.5% of the time (precision 0.125 for that predicate), weakly (0.03-0.15 relative magnitude in the misses). At recall_idx 1 it is never active (precision 0). The qualitative claim (silent or weak) holds.
Test scores reproduce: precision 0.998, recall 0.962, F1 0.979, mass recall 0.993. The lowest activation quartile has 0.85 coverage, explained by the weak recall_idx-2 v hits.
Per-position check holds: for v at recall_idx 3, 4, 6 and 8, precision is 0.99-1.0. Activations in the original phase and at the delimiter are exactly 0.

There are about 150 activations on non-v inputs (x, t, 3, e and others) out of about 60k, and the 134 test false positives are v at recall_idx 3 that stays silent. Neither forms a systematic class; both are scattered noise.
The 'peaks late (to_go 0-1)' claim is mildly supported: to_go 0 holds 34% of activation mass with 28% of active steps. The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
